review: Second intensive review; source execution paths, not reputation or names, decide verdicts.

execution: Copies /bin/sh to /usr/bin/dbus-authd, changes owner to root, then adds the setuid bit. This is retained privileged access, not an initial exploit; the shell may require privilege-preserving invocation.

A quoted heredoc writes literal post_boot.d hook source. At a subsequent hook execution it conditionally appends passwordless ALL sudo permission to an appliance template and invokes bt-sysconfig. The initial script does not execute that hook.
Two bt-secrets get calls request the credential vault on inherited stdout. No network exfiltration occurs in this file.
Deletes the vault audit log and rotations, then active authentication, HTTP, application and system logs. No set -e: later actions are attempted even after earlier failures.
samples.context_limits: Requires the appliance paths, tools and existing write/root authority. No deployment authorization, exploit, actor or CVE is established. Combined retained root access, secret retrieval and record erasure tip the verdict.
samples.changes: None: all 29 findings retained, including two hostile and six suspicious findings.

samples.identification: PowerShell remote encoded-source job stager; claimed ChocoShell attribution unverified
execution: Changes this process execution policy to Bypass, then attempts three HTTPS status requests to an external IP. The status strings are fixed labels, not evidence of administrator checks or key recovery.
Queries Win32_ShadowCopy through WMI; the result is unused. Builds a Chrome History pathname; never opens, copies or reads the database.

Downloads two strings. The tooling string is unused. The stager string flows through FromBase64String and UTF8.GetString into ScriptBlock.Create, then that same block is submitted to Start-Job. No signature/authenticity verification or user confirmation guards that chain.

POSTs only the interpolated history pathname. This reveals a local profile path; it is not credential or history-content theft. No supplied encrypted or encoded literal payload exists to decode locally.
samples.context_limits: Remote response and subsequent payload are unavailable; HTTPS or job success is not assumed. No actor or family attribution is independently established. Remote decoded code execution with policy bypass, operational callbacks, and browser-path disclosure outweigh a legitimate installer interpretation.
samples.coverage: Two suspicious objectives cover linked encoded-source execution and remote-job activation with process policy bypass. Neutral job/deployment observations remain notable.
samples.changes: Removed two unsupported hostile URL/construction composites. Preserved and generalized the asset-route reference in its neutral path home. Relocated the beacon word without changing matcher or severity.

execution: main calls installPersistence and beacon once each. installPersistence joins LOCALAPPDATA to a directory and writes the string installed to .svchost32mid with mode 0644; it does not create the parent directory and ignores write errors.

The executable path is only printed. InstallPath, ServiceDescription and MarkerFileUl constants are unused. No executable copy/write, service registration, service start, registry access, autorun change or privilege escalation occurs.

beacon performs one GET to https://192.142.52.31:443/api/v1/ping. It neither reads the response nor repeats requests nor handles received commands. A C2Address variable name does not establish a command channel.

An isolated Go test executes the unchanged source main with LOCALAPPDATA in a disposable directory and a captured in-memory HTTP transport. It observes only the marker and one GET, with zero response-body reads. No network request leaves the harness.
samples.context_limits: The endpoint purpose and real deployment are unknown. The weak backdoor/persistence names and unused configuration resemble a demonstration; the reachable implementation lacks those advertised capabilities. That positive source evidence tips BENIGN, not an absence of scanner hits. The scanner flow-query-incomplete warning is addressed by manual inspection of all functions.
samples.changes: Removed unsupported hostile service-install/masquerade and beacon composites. Preserved the exact executable-path and description matchers as neutral observations, reducing the bare path from suspicious to notable because no drop/install is required.

shared_rule_review.consumers: No consumers of the removed CornFlake or ChocoShell composite IDs were found. Exact and ancestor YAML references were searched before changes. Referencing Cobalt Strike, Melofee, WordPress, Elex, and path-breakout rules were updated for relocated observations without changing their Boolean conditions.
shared_rule_review.independent_positives: No independent supplied source sample contains the CornFlake marker set or ChocoShell asset path. Existing appliance post-exploit (17 controls), Go browser/autorun (9 controls), and an actual browser-history-export fixture were inspected and checked. Realistic source-only service creation/staging still yields hostile service persistence and masquerade findings. No true attack technique was represented by the removed string-pair-only composites.
shared_rule_review.capacity_and_placement: A bare WinWord name moved from executable paths to basename references; encoded shell-breakout URL literals moved from neutral HTTP paths to command injection. These correct existing placement while keeping canonical destination budgets. Matchers/scopes/severities are preserved.
shared_rule_review.ancestor_exception: The Ruby HTTP/write/launch profile excludes the old HTTP path directory. Moving its attack-specific shell-breakout member to objectives deliberately stops that particular attack literal from suppressing the neutral Ruby profile; adding an objectives dependency to a micro-behavior is prohibited. No hostile finding is lost; a Ruby file can gain an accurate notable co-occurrence observation.
shared_rule_review.remaining_legacy_paths: Other accurate HTTP capabilities retain admitted existing legacy homes while their documented taxonomy migrations remain open; no new rule is added to a legacy library namespace.
